newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian tobacco tycoon confirms Astra buying.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian tobacco tycoon confirms Astra buying.

text.p: Indonesian tobacco tycoon Putera Sampoerna is at least partly involved in a strong wave of buying into the country's largest car manufacturer Astra International, an aide said on Wednesday.
"It is true that Putera Sampoerna has bought some shares of Astra International," said Ditta Amahoerseya, corporate public relations manager of cigarette giant PT Hanjaya Putra Mandala Sampoerna.
She said Sampoerna bought some shares from Henry Pribadi, another Indonesian tycoon, but declined to give details of how many and at what price.
Astra shares have risen sharply over the past week on rumours that it is likely to be a takeover target.
Amahoerseya said Sampoerna was attracted by the low prevailing price of Astra shares. "The price was cheap and it's good for investment," she added.
She declined to comment on whether Sampoerna was planning to buy additional shares from other shareholders or from Pribadi.
"He did not buy all of Pribadi's shares, only some of it," she said.
Brokers say Pribadi holds about a three percent stake in Astra, which is 8.26 percent owned by Toyota Motor Corp.
Astra shares were trading at 3,725 rupiah late on Wednesday, up from 2,625 on September 16 before rumours of the takeover surfaced.
